title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 532
text:
30. Approximately 50 countries afford legal recognition to a transgender person’s “gender
identity”. However, in many countries, trans people are excluded by society, and may face
widespread discrimination, prosecution, harassment and violence.

31. People who face persecution on the basis of their gender identity can claim asylum in Britain.
The Gender Recognition Act 2004

32. The GRA 2004 enables trans people to change their legal gender/sex on their birth
certificate by applying to the Gender Recognition Panel for a GRC. The Gender Recognition
Panel is a judicial body comprising legal and medical members. Since the GRA 2004 came
into force on 4 April 2005, over 5,500 people have been granted a GRC.

33. The panel must grant the application for a GRC if it is satisfied that the applicant has or has
had “gender dysphoria”, has lived in the “acquired gender” (as gender identity is referred to
in the GRA 2004) for two years, intends to continue to live in the acquired gender for the rest
of their lives and complies with certain evidential and medical requirements.
